title: Moscow Gets a Patriarch and Calls Itself the Third Rome
dek: In 1589 the patriarch of Constantinople installs Job as Moscow's first patriarch, in a charter that names Russia the Third Rome. In 2018 the two churches split over Kyiv.
body: Two Romes have fallen, a Pskov monk wrote, and a fourth there shall not be. Four centuries on, Moscow and Constantinople still contest who leads the Orthodox world.

panels.label: Moscow's Synod Said
panels.text: In 2018 Moscow’s Holy Synod said Constantinople’s Ukraine decisions were an “encroachment on someone else’s canonical regions” and broke communion with it.

panels.label: Constantinople's Synod Said
panels.text: In 2018 Constantinople’s Holy Synod said the 1686 letter letting Moscow ordain Kyiv’s metropolitan was “issued for the circumstances of that time” and revoked it.

panels.label: The Stakes
panels.text: Both churches cite old charters; at stake is who ranks first in Orthodoxy, and whether the church in Kyiv answers to Moscow or stands on its own.
